start.starsNote: Decision 6a: the original started every hotel at 3 stars, and 3 is the floor. computeStars returns 3 for a fresh hotel by construction (see stars.json).

simulation.offlineNote: Two different things, kept apart. analyticThroughputFactor corrects a MODELLING error: the closed-form resolver assumes perfect packing. Re-measured with tools/balance-sim/offline-parity.ts after 3B moved the catalogue to the original tables (2-4 minute stays, 1-10 coin incomes): undiscounted mean 1.118 across five hotel sizes and two windows, so the correction is 0.895. offlineEfficiency is a DESIGN LEVER: how much less an unwatched hotel earns, on purpose. Re-measure after any change to arrivals, capacity or reception. ADDENDUM (3A, decision 10a-supplement pending sign-off): maxOfflineHours raised 14 -> 48. The original never truncated a paid shift — the shift end IS the offline cap — and a 14h daily cap under original prices made every long shift a guaranteed loss (a 48h shift cost 14,145+ while only 14h of it could ever pay). 48 matches the longest shift, and resolveOffline still stops at shiftEnd.

guests.checkInNote: Check-in takes checkInSec / receptionistEfficiency seconds. 4B: an unstaffed desk is worked by a TEMP at full speed — temps are complete workers whose cost is the temp wage in shiftWages, exactly the original model — so requireReceptionist stays false and tempReceptionistEfficiency is 1.

decorMeter.note: final income multiplier = 1 + lerp(emptyIncomePenalty, maxIncomeBonusAtFull, fillRatio)

xp.note: build/decor grants are a fraction of the item cost

satisfaction.note: Satisfaction = clamp(base + quality + cleanliness + service + amenity - wait - incident - unmet, 0, 100). Weights are the maximum each term can contribute. tipMaxRatio caps the bonus a delighted guest adds to their bill. Provisional — Phase 6 tunes.

roomQuality.note: Decision 8b: quality = fill with diminishing returns on repeats (repeatFalloff stays, guarding the original's documented cheapest-item exploit); the variety requirement is neutralised by varietyFloor=1. Condition (hazards) still gates income elsewhere. Equipment (appliances and storage) is the mirror of the bed rule: a treadmill belongs in a room that works, never in a bedroom.

upkeep.note: Decision 10a: upkeep is not in the original; zeroed so the shift price IS the original table. Field kept for the schema. The original balanced its sinks through expansion prices and the weekly catalogue instead.

poke.note: Decision 3a: tapping a sleeping guest pays a uniform 400..500 once per guest, capped per day. The cap value is ours to tune — the snapshot documents the range and the existence of a daily limit, not its size.
